name: the Botanic Garden
title: Ancient Trees in Cambridge's Botanic Garden: 5 to Find
meta_description: Darwin's teacher planted pines to look wrong. Cambridge's Botanic Garden holds a storm-felled thicket and Britain's first dawn redwood.
intro: John Stevens Henslow, the botanist who mentored Charles Darwin, set out the Botanic Garden's Main Walk with black pines facing each other in pairs, where a visitor expects symmetry, and chose trees that refuse to match. Nearby, a Caucasian wingnut that a storm brought down in 1886 was never cleared. The gardeners let the suckers come up, and the thicket now straddling the stream has stems as tall as the original tree. The garden calls its dawn redwood by the Lake the first to grow on British soil since the Mesozoic. Its seed was collected in China in 1946 and 1947, and two seedlings went into the ground in 1949. Two pines in the collection are champion trees, a Chilgoza pine that was 5.4 metres in 1915 and is 14.4 now, and a single-leaf nut pine that a storm in 2000 heaved out of the ground and which came to rest on a low branch and kept growing. Most ages here are not documented, and several of the trees are rarities more than veterans.
